anti_duplication_rules: Statewide StateCivics PostgreSQL and existing custody/source-ledger services remain canonical. ExAIS stores only rebuildable scoped projections; no second canonical graph, provider, graph engine, global policy or direct authoritative upstream write.

KS-600/T-001 alone defines provision identity, field-combination/evidence interpretation, snapshot selection and authority arithmetic in provision-reference.schema.json and appropriation_reconciler.py. ExAIS consumes exact canonical results/derivations; never port arithmetic, sum snippets, or add an action amount to its linked fact.

Native derivation inputs are {type,id,revision_or_hash}; native outputs are {type,id,hash_sha256}. JSON-schema optional/null output hashes are insufficient for reviewed lineage: require the supported hash required by typed record/ORM. Preserve ordered input/output set hashes and run context. Normalized projection refs retain original shape; no symmetric-storage rewrite, appropriation_action_id fact field, second lineage table, or Cartesian input/output edges.

Canonical provision version identity is separate from display numbering, source spans, re-extraction and observation/effective time. KS-601 owns reviewed effective-dated account crosswalks; equal codes/labels, section numbers, similarity or unresolved statute History cannot create identity or edges. Unknown dates/subunits/matches remain unknown.

KS-650/T-002 extends only the existing retrieval exporter/schema/CLI with explicit kind/version dispatch. Keep legacy document records/bytes compatible. Never require the provisional ExAIS publisher v1 envelope upstream or build a second exporter/ledger/locator pipeline. Fill only idempotent missing evidence through existing services; no copied CSV corpus, fake PDFs or harvest restart.

KS-650 owns the bounded compatible publication-record.subject_type fiscal extension coordinated with KS-605. Existing allowed subject types exclude fiscal entities; never mislabel them. Actual reviewed publication and nonrevoked snapshot/source records are prerequisites; schemas alone are not producer/readiness proof and unrelated entire epics are not gates.

T-004 alone owns FiscalCanonicalReference, FiscalEvidenceCitation, FiscalEntityResult, FiscalProjectionBatch, FiscalProjectionPartition, FiscalProjectionManifest and response model extensions in schemas.py. T-005/006/007 import these; do not redeclare dict/envelope/citation variants or manufacture document/chunk IDs for structured evidence.

T-004 owns generation/partition identity and complete-manifest validation through fiscal_graph_artifact.py:validate_fiscal_projection_manifest and fiscal_graph.py:guard_fiscal_graph_generation. Every declared partition/count/hash and cross-partition endpoint must resolve; keep 1000-node/2000-edge per-batch bounds. New bill/FY generations explicitly include all retained approved partitions; never silently replace another bill or truncate.

T-005 owns active pointer transitions and durable lifecycle denial; it consumes the T-004 immutable manifest validator and does not duplicate it. Stage all counts/hash/source/profile/index acknowledgements before scoped compare-and-swap. Failed/partial stages preserve the prior approved view; rollback rechecks current rights/tombstones and never resurrects denied material.

T-005 alone defines fiscal_projection.py:fiscal_record_eligible. Ordinary graph-off/unscoped requests, dense/sparse/exact lookup, traversal and citations must use trusted server-derived fiscal scope and refreshed canonical eligibility. Backend filters are defense in depth; stale vector points, graph disablement, omitted client metadata or late external awaits cannot bypass final hydration/serialization checks.

T-006 stewards RetrievalService.search/answer and five-mode dispatch; T-005 installs mandatory eligibility hooks first, T-006 integrates retrieval second, T-007 adds audit measurements last.
